Plot vector contours or properties

Source: R/images.R
plot.mlv_drawing.Rd

Draws the drawing on its canvas in image coordinates (x rightward, y downward, equal aspect ratio). The canvas spans the raster extent, 0.5 to `width + 0.5` and 0.5 to `height + 0.5`, because pixel centres lie at integers starting at 1; the plot coordinates are those of [plot.mlv_mat()], so MAT stages and drawings overlay exactly. With a `property`, segments are coloured by that quantity and, by default, a colour bar naming the quantity and its unit is drawn to the right of the canvas, inside the plot region, so later low-level calls (`points()`, `text()`) use the same coordinates.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mlv_drawing'
plot(
  x,
  property = NULL,
  col = "black",
  lwd = 1,
  ...,
  legend = TRUE,
  palette = NULL,
  zlim = NULL,
  arms = FALSE,
  arm_length = NULL,
  junction_col = "#D55E00",
  frame = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

A drawing.

property

Optional segment property (`"orientation"`, `"length"`, `"curvature"`), `"junctions"`, or a mapped MAT property.

col

Contour colour when no segment property is shown.

lwd

Line width.

...

Arguments to the initial plot, such as `main`, `xlim` or `axes = FALSE`.

legend

Draw a colour bar when colour encodes a quantity.

palette

Optional palette: a function of the number of colours, or a character vector of colours. Defaults are described above.

zlim

Value range mapped onto the palette for length and curvature; values outside it take the end colours. Defaults to the finite data range. Ignored for orientation (always 0 to 180 degrees) and MAT scores (0 to 1).

arms

Draw junction arms.

arm_length

Drawn arm length in pixels; defaults to 8 canvas side.

junction_col

Colour of junction markers and arms.

frame

Outline the canvas in light grey.

Value

The drawing invisibly.

Details

Orientation is axial: a segment at 10 degrees and one at 190 degrees have the same colour, and the default palette is a cyclic hue wheel over 0 to 180 degrees, so 0 and 180 share a colour. Length and curvature use the sequential Viridis palette over `zlim`. Mapped medial-axis scores are drawn as filled mapped pixels on a 0 to 1 Viridis scale over grey contours. With `property = "junctions"`, or `arms = TRUE`, junction positions are marked; `arms = TRUE` also draws each arm as an arrow leaving the junction along its orientation (the `arms` column of [detect_junctions()]). Junctions come from the drawing's stored `junctions` (for example from [compute_contour_properties()] with `rule = "mlv2023"`), its feature specification, or default [detect_junctions()].

Examples

d <- mlv_drawing(list(rbind(c(5, 10, 35, 10)), rbind(c(20, 10, 20, 35))), 40, 40)
plot(d, property = "orientation")

plot(d, property = "junctions", arms = TRUE, axes = FALSE)
